sections.heading: Boxes Sized to Garments, Not Guesswork
sections.text: Fashion Brand Packaging Boxes Sized to Garments, Not Guesswork Apparel packaging fails in boring ways: boxes a size too big so the fold collapses in transit, interiors that snag knits, lids that crush under stacking. We size each box to the folded garment spec — tees, hoodies, denim, scarves — so the piece arrives showroom-folded. The tissue system is part of the design: colour-matched sheets pre-folded to the box, sealed with your branded sticker. Interiors are smooth-lined with no exposed board edges to catch loops or silk. The magnetic lid opens flat for the reveal shot. Cream, black and kraft are stocked; any Pantone from 500 pcs. Ships flat option available for volume programs (see collapsible magnetic boxes ). Explore the fashion packaging solutions page .

sections.heading: What Should a Candle Gift Box Protect?
sections.text: Buyer Answer What Should a Candle Gift Box Protect? Short answer: Design the box around the filled jar, not an empty container drawing. The insert must limit side movement, support the jar without loading the lid or wick, leave a practical finger-removal path, and be tested with the finished pack. Jar weight, glass profile, insert material and courier route all affect the final specification.

sections.heading: Approve the Jar, Insert and Box as One System
sections.text: Packaged-Product Validation Approve the Jar, Insert and Box as One System A candle carton cannot be qualified from board thickness alone. Record the filled jar mass, maximum body diameter, shoulder and base profile, lid projection and the points that may safely contact an insert. A collar that looks tight around an empty jar can become difficult to remove after filling, while a loose collar lets the glass build momentum before impact. The International Safe Transit Association explains that packaged-product testing evaluates the product and package together, and recommends retesting when the product, package, material, component or distribution system changes. Use that principle during sampling: approve movement, removal and visible damage criteria with the exact production jar and candle. See ISTA retesting guidance . Send one filled, closed production jar for each size and weight family. Mark surfaces that may not be rubbed, compressed or touched by the insert. Define whether the presentation box ships inside a corrugated mailer or acts as the shipping pack. Repeat the agreed check when the jar, lid, insert, board or delivery route changes.

sections.heading: Send These Details for a Buildable Candle-Box Quote
sections.text: RFQ Checklist Send These Details for a Buildable Candle-Box Quote Filled jar dimensions, weight, lid profile and one physical sample per family. Single, twin, trio or discovery-set layout and required removal direction. Retail presentation box only, or presentation box plus courier shipper. Destination market, parcel route, damage criteria and sustainability restrictions. Order quantity, artwork coverage, finish, insert preference and target launch date. Worked approval example A brand using one outer box for two candle scents should not assume the same insert because both labels list the same fill weight. One jar may have a thicker base, wider shoulder or different lid overhang. The approval record should name the exact jar version, filled weight, insert revision and outer-box revision, then state the allowed movement, removal method and visible-damage limit. If only the fragrance changes and every physical component remains identical, the signed pack can remain the reference. If the glass supplier, jar profile, lid, wax fill, insert material or delivery route changes, review the pack again before releasing the next run. This turns “protect the candle” into a repeatable purchasing decision instead of an unsupported promise. Also separate presentation approval from transit approval. Colour, foil position and the unboxing reveal can be signed off on a presentation sample, while courier protection must be judged with the filled jar and any outer shipper. Recording both decisions prevents a visually approved prototype from being treated as proof of distribution performance.

sections.text: Assembly & Freight Specification Approve the Fold, Finished Size and Packed Shipment Together AI-generated illustrative concept only; not a measured packing trial, assembly record or freight-savings result. A useful freight comparison needs measurements of the finished box, supplied folded unit and packed export carton for the same project. An opened-panel drawing or dieline is not the folded-unit shipping size. Use this checklist in the RFQ and sample approval. Record sample ID, revision, measurement date, packing mode, units per carton and measured outer carton dimensions. Carton CBM = L x W x H / 1,000,000,000 for mm, or / 1,000,000 for cm; total CBM is the sum across all cartons. Do not infer freight savings from CBM alone. Check the carrier's chargeable-weight rules and destination assembly work. Measure the loaded fit , select the insert and wrap , and use the same-specification quote comparison . Request a written specification review or compare the standard magnetic rigid format .

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Frequently Asked Questions Straight answers from our factory team — MOQ, lead time, finishes and protection. How does a collapsible magnetic gift box save on shipping? sections.heading: EVA, Paperboard or Molded Pulp — the Kit's Real Cost Driver
sections.text: Insert Decision EVA, Paperboard or Molded Pulp — the Kit's Real Cost Driver On a multi-item kit the box is rarely what decides the unit cost. The insert is: it sets the tooling bill, the assembly time and, increasingly, whether the recipient's employer can put the kit through a recycling policy. EVA foam Paperboard Molded pulp Holds irregular shapes Best — precise cavities Weakest — folds and dividers only Good — molded to the form Tooling Low, easy to revise Die only Mould required, longer lead time Where it wins on cost Small runs, spec still changing Simple layouts Repeat high-volume programs End of life Limited recyclability in standard streams Curbside recyclable Recyclable in paper streams, compostable The trade-off is well documented across the trade: EVA is efficient for precise cavities and small revisions, paperboard is cost-effective when the structure is simple but complex folding adds labour, and molded pulp needs tooling and a longer lead time yet becomes efficient on repeated high-volume programs . Read that as a decision rule rather than a preference: if your kit contents are still being negotiated internally, EVA keeps you flexible. Once the kit is locked and you are reordering it every quarter, pulp starts winning on both cost and the sustainability line item. One factor that catches procurement teams out — molded pulp reportedly ships around 40% more compactly than plastic foams . On an air-freighted onboarding kit going to several countries, that difference lands on the freight invoice, not the packaging invoice, which is why it usually gets missed in a like-for-like unit-price comparison.

sections.heading: Kitting Is Labour, and Labour Is the Line Nobody Budgets
sections.text: Programme Planning Kitting Is Labour, and Labour Is the Line Nobody Budgets A five-item kit is not five times a one-item box. Every additional SKU in the cavity adds a pick, a placement and an orientation check per unit, and that time multiplies by your whole run. Three consequences worth planning around before you sign off a kit design: Cavity design is an assembly-speed decision. A cavity that only accepts its item one way round is slower to fill than one that accepts it either way — but it is the one that guarantees the unboxing looks identical on every unit. Choose deliberately: symmetry where presentation allows it, keyed cavities only where orientation genuinely matters. Mixed-SKU kits need a reconciliation plan. If your kit contains a size-variable item — apparel in S/M/L, or a regional power adapter — the run splits into variants, and each variant needs its own pack-out, carton label and count. Decide the variant split before production, not during. Client-supplied items change the timeline. If part of the kit ships to us for insertion, the whole programme waits on the slowest inbound item. Confirm arrival dates for supplied goods before we schedule the assembly window, and build in buffer for customs on anything crossing a border to reach us. A practical rule for corporate calendars: an onboarding or event kit that must land on a fixed date should have its contents frozen well before the box is signed off, because a content change after tooling means either new tooling or a compromise cavity. Both cost more than the meeting that would have locked the list.

sections.text: Packaging applications Candle and diffuser gift set packaging: planning the fit For a candle and diffuser gift box, review the candle jar, bottle and reed length together before choosing outer dimensions. The illustrated candle and aromatherapy layout is a starting concept; a diffuser-and-reed version needs its own fitted sample. Packaging scope covers the box and agreed insert, not candles, oils or accessories. Multi-compartment candle gift boxes Keep glass items in separate cavities. Check the full jar diameter, lid height and packed weight; assess retention using the actual filled products rather than empty containers alone. Reed diffuser gift box inserts Account for the bottle closure and the complete reed bundle. A long reed compartment may change the box footprint. Review removal access and avoid loading the lid against fragile bottle components. Choose the insert and shipping pack together Compare EVA retention with paperboard dividers against the real product weight and presentation needs. A fitted display tray does not by itself prove parcel-shipping protection. Validate the complete box, transit carton and cushioning with the intended delivery method. sections.heading: Which Corrugated Specification Belongs on an RFQ?
sections.text: Buyer Answer Which Corrugated Specification Belongs on an RFQ? Short answer: Specify the packed product, inside dimensions, total weight, stacking and parcel route before naming a flute. ECT describes edgewise board resistance; it does not by itself guarantee finished-box compression. The converter still needs liner and medium construction, flute profile, box style, joint, print process, conditioning and an agreed packed-box test.

sections.heading: Use ECT as a Material Input, Not a Shipping Guarantee
sections.text: Board vs Box Performance Use ECT as a Material Input, Not a Shipping Guarantee ISO 3037:2022 defines a non-waxed-edge method for measuring edgewise crush resistance of corrugated fibreboard, with force applied in the flute direction. That is a repeatable board test. Finished-case performance also changes with box dimensions, score quality, slots, manufacturer's joint, print/lamination, humidity, packing pattern and how the load reaches the panels. For sourcing, provide a performance brief and ask the converter to return the proposed board construction plus the packed-box verification route. Do not copy an ECT value from a competitor carton without matching its size, contents and supply chain. State product dimensions, packed weight and unsupported voids. Separate retail-display requirements from parcel or pallet requirements. Identify moisture exposure, cold chain or long warehouse dwell. Approve the converted sample after print, die-cutting and joint formation.

sections.heading: Send Inputs That Let the Supplier Engineer the Board
sections.text: RFQ Checklist Send Inputs That Let the Supplier Engineer the Board Inside dimensions, packed weight, product orientation and void locations. Parcel, pallet, retail-ready or mixed distribution route. Stack height, storage duration, humidity exposure and failure criteria. Required print process, ink coverage, coating, barcode and colour tolerances. Order quantity, delivery market and whether packed-box testing is required. Worked specification example Two buyers can request the same inside dimensions and still need different cases. A light retail product shipped one unit at a time may value print surface and dimensional efficiency; a denser product stacked for weeks may place more demand on panel and corner performance. The RFQ should therefore pair dimensions with packed weight, stacking pattern, warehouse duration, route and acceptable damage. The converter can then return a proposed flute and board construction, but approval still belongs to the converted and packed sample. Record the sample's board identification, box style, joint, print route, closure and conditioning state so a later repeat order is compared with the same reference. This also prevents a board-strength number from being copied into a purchase order without the conditions that made it meaningful. Print method belongs in the same record. Direct flexographic print, coated liner and litho-lamination can change surface appearance, converting behaviour and moisture response. Approve colour, barcode and structure on the route being purchased, then keep the signed sample and board identification together. A later artwork-only change can follow that reference; a board, flute, joint or laminate change needs a fresh comparison.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions Is ECT the same as finished-box compression strength? No. ISO 3037 measures edgewise resistance of corrugated fibreboard; finished-box performance also depends on dimensions, style, joint, converting, environment and packed load. Should I choose E flute or B flute? Choose from product weight, protection, print surface, dimensions and route, then compare the proposed converted samples instead of selecting by flute name alone. When is litho-laminated corrugated useful? It is useful when retail graphics need finer reproduction on a corrugated structure; approve laminate bond, warp, colour, barcode and packed performance together. How should humidity be handled in the specification? State storage and delivery exposure in the RFQ and qualify the proposed construction under agreed conditions because paper-based performance changes with moisture. What inputs are needed for a corrugated-box quote? Send inside dimensions, packed weight, orientation, route, stacking and storage needs, print coverage, barcode criteria, quantity, market and required packed-box evidence.

sections.heading: The Secure, Eco-Conscious Choice for Modern D2C Sourcing
sections.text: High-Performance Mailers The Secure, Eco-Conscious Choice for Modern D2C Sourcing The corrugated mailer box with an integrated tear strip represents the ultimate evolution of standard shipping boxes. Crafted from highly dense corrugated fluting sandwiched between durable kraft liners, this structural packaging offers immense crush resistance without the need for additional shipping envelopes. By integrating a high-tension tearing ribbon, your customers enjoy a clean, satisfying unboxing experience that completely eliminates the safety hazard of using knives, scissors, or keys to cut through packing tape. Furthermore, our dual peel-and-seal tape design features a second adhesive line, allowing customers to easily reuse the exact same box for shipping returns or exchanges without tape waste. At LuxoPack, we utilize advanced digital and offset flexographic printing presses to deliver crisp imagery and accurate color reproduction. From minimalist outer branding to rich inside-the-box storyboards, we construct mailers that keep your products secure and your branding memorable during transit.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What are the benefits of corrugated mailer boxes with tear strips? They provide a premium, tool-free unboxing experience for your customers while increasing security during transit. The tear strip is tamper-evident, ensuring the customer is the first to open the package. Dual-peel-and-seal strips also make returns simple and eco-friendly by reusing the exact same box. What corrugated board thickness and flute grades do you offer? We primarily manufacture mailers using high-density E-Flute (1.6mm thickness) for its crisp fold lines and excellent puncture resistance, which is perfect for most cosmetics, subscription kits, and apparel shipping. For heavier products, we provide B-Flute (3.2mm) and heavy-duty double-wall boards. Can we print on both the inside and outside of the mailer box? Yes. We specialize in high-definition inside-and-outside printing. You can customize the exterior with minimal eco-friendly branding and flood-coat the interior with vivid Pantone spot colors, custom typography, or localized patterns to surprise customers upon opening. What is the MOQ for custom corrugated mailers with tear strips? Our minimum order quantity for completely bespoke sizes and double-sided printing with custom easy-tear strips is 300 units, allowing scaling e-commerce brands to benefit from direct factory pricing without large inventories. Do you provide FSC certified and eco-friendly materials? Absolutely. All our cardboard materials are sourced from FSC-certified forests, meaning they are completely recyclable, renewable, and biodegradable. We use soy-based inks and eco-friendly water-based protective varnishes.

sections.heading: The 360° Branded Cylinder That Owns the Shelf
sections.text: Round Paper Tube Packaging The 360° Branded Cylinder That Owns the Shelf A cylinder tube box wraps your product in a continuous, seam-aware 360° printed surface — no flat front, no dead panels. That uninterrupted canvas is why premium candle, tea, coffee, spirits and skincare brands choose round tube packaging to stand apart from the sea of square cartons. Our tubes are spiral-wound from rigid paperboard (not flimsy single-ply card), so the wall holds its shape, resists denting in transit, and gives a reassuring weight in hand. Ends are configured to your product: snug paperboard lids, brushed-metal caps, clear PET windows, or shoulder-and-neck telescoping closures. Every tube is produced in-house from board winding to wrap lamination, so registration stays crisp around the full circumference and the top/bottom seams sit flush. Add gold foil, soft-touch matte, embossed logos or a tear-strip opening to finish the unboxing.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What is a cylinder tube box made of? Our cylinder tubes are spiral-wound from rigid paperboard (1.2mm–2.5mm wall), then wrapped with your printed art paper or kraft. This makes a sturdy, dent-resistant round box — far stronger than single-ply card tubes — with paperboard, metal, wood or window end caps. What is the minimum order quantity for custom tube packaging? Standard MOQ is 200 pcs for a custom diameter with full 360° wrap printing. Smaller pilot runs can be discussed for premium projects. Can tube boxes be food-grade for tea, coffee or supplements? Yes. We offer food-grade inner liners and aluminium-foil liners that preserve aroma and meet food-contact requirements for loose-leaf tea, coffee beans, bath salts and capsules. Do you offer eco-friendly / recyclable paper tubes? Yes. We produce plastic-free, mono-material paper tubes using FSC-certified board, paperboard ends and water-based coatings so the whole tube is recyclable. What end caps and openings are available? Paperboard push-fit lids, brushed-metal aluminium caps, wooden lids, clear PET windows, telescoping shoulder-neck closures, and easy-tear strips.

sections.text: Retail Carton Program The Workhorse Box, Printed Like a Premium One Folding cartons carry much of retail because they combine printable surfaces with flat delivery and efficient conversion. Offset lithography can hold gradients and brand colour, but repeatability still needs an approved colour target, substrate and finish rather than a universal tolerance claim. Structures cover the tuck family: straight-tuck, reverse-tuck, auto-lock bottom, hang-tab tops and window variants. Board options include named SBS, FBB and recycled grades; the correct choice depends on surface, stiffness, fibre requirement and product duty. Soft-touch lamination, spot UV, foil and emboss can change both appearance and score response, so approve them on the finished structural sample. For heavier shipping duty see corrugated boxes ; for peg retail see hang tab boxes .

sections.heading: How Do You Specify a Folding Carton?
sections.text: Buyer Answer How Do You Specify a Folding Carton? Short answer: Start with the packed product, retail channel, print standard and closure duty, then select the paperboard. SBS, FBB and recycled grades differ in surface, stiffness, bulk and fibre composition, but the trade name alone is not enough. Quote caliper, grain direction, structure, coating, print coverage, packed weight and the sample checks that decide acceptance.

sections.heading: Board Name, Caliper and Grain Solve Different Problems
sections.text: Paperboard Qualification Board Name, Caliper and Grain Solve Different Problems The Paperboard Packaging Council describes folding cartons as converted paperboard structures made from virgin or recycled grades and notes that they fold flat for storage and shipping. That efficiency does not remove the need to qualify stiffness, score response and surface for the actual carton. Ask for a named mill grade or an approved equivalent, not only “white card.” Confirm which direction the grain runs relative to the main folds, because a visually identical layout can fold and bow differently when imposed in the other direction. Heavy ink, lamination and foil also change score behaviour, so approve a printed, finished structural sample rather than a blank white dummy alone. State direct-food-contact or migration requirements before choosing recycled or virgin board. Define shelf hang, tuck, crash-lock, auto-bottom or glued-seam duty. Put barcode grade, colour tolerance and rub resistance into acceptance criteria. Check filled-carton squareness, opening force and closure after conditioning.

sections.heading: Inputs for a Folding-Carton Dieline and Quote
sections.text: RFQ Checklist Inputs for a Folding-Carton Dieline and Quote Product dimensions, packed weight, loading method and closure requirement. Retail channel, shelf orientation, hang-tab or tamper-evidence need. Named board grade or performance target, caliper and fibre-content requirement. Print standard, coating, foil, emboss, window, barcode and rub criteria. Order quantity, flat or erected delivery, packing line and destination compliance. Worked qualification example A skincare carton with dense dark ink, soft-touch lamination and a foil panel should be approved in its finished form. A blank structural sample can confirm dimensions and loading, but it cannot reveal whether the printed sheet cracks on the main score, whether the laminate lifts near a lock, or whether glue bonds reliably to the selected surface. Record the mill grade or approved equivalent, caliper, grain direction, print coverage, coating, foil area, crease rule and closure. Then fill the carton with the production-weight item and check squareness, panel bow, opening and closing, barcode readability and visible rub after handling. If a substitute board is proposed later, treat it as a controlled change and compare it against the signed finished sample rather than accepting an acronym or grammage alone. Flat-delivery efficiency should be reviewed with the buyer's packing line. A carton that stores compactly can still add labour if the lock is difficult to erect or if the tuck catches during filling. Include erection method, line speed, operator access and closure sequence in the sample review so the structural choice works in production as well as on shelf.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions Should I specify SBS, FBB or recycled paperboard? Start with print, stiffness, surface, fibre-content and compliance needs, then approve a named grade or equivalent; the acronym alone is not a complete specification. Why does grain direction matter? Grain direction changes fold response and panel shape, so record it with the dieline and approve the finished carton in the imposed production direction. How do you check score cracking? Review the printed, coated and finished sample at the real folds because ink, lamination, foil, board and crease settings work as one system. Which closure should I choose? Select tuck, lock-bottom, auto-bottom or glued construction from product weight, packing method, line speed, opening experience and tamper requirements. What inputs are needed for a folding-carton quote? Send product size and weight, loading and closure, board requirement, print and finish, barcode criteria, quantity, packing line, delivery form and destination compliance.

sections.heading: Tabs That Hold, Faces That Sell

Windows show the product; hang-and-stand hybrid bases let the same SKU work pegs and shelves. Related: folding cartons and phone case retail boxes .

sections.heading: The Shape That Says It Before You Open It
sections.text: Die-Formed Heart Rigid Box The Shape That Says It Before You Open It A heart-shaped box carries emotional meaning the moment it is seen — which is why it is the default choice for proposals, Valentine, weddings and romantic jewelry gifting. The challenge is making the curved silhouette clean and structural, not flimsy; that is what our die-forming and hand-wrapping process delivers. Each heart box is built on a rigid board frame wrapped in soft-touch, velvet-texture or art paper, with crisp seams around the curves and a flush lid line. Choose a flip-top hinge or a lift-off clamshell, finished with a satin ribbon pull, gold foil monogram or blind emboss. Inside, a custom velvet insert holds rings, pendants or a chocolate tray securely, so the gift presents perfectly on opening. Available in any brand colour — blush, red, black, ivory — with matching ribbon.

sections.heading: Match the Handle to the Weight, Not to the Mood Board
sections.text: Load Engineering Match the Handle to the Weight, Not to the Mood Board Nearly every paper bag failure is the same failure: the handle was chosen for how it looked in the render, and the product turned out heavier than the render implied. Handle type is a load spec first and an aesthetic second. Handle Indicative load Where it belongs Die-cut (punched) Light only Cosmetics samples, cards, short carry from counter to car Twisted paper Roughly 5–8 kg (12–18 lb) depending on construction Apparel, everyday retail Cotton or nylon rope Roughly 15–25 kg Multi-item gifting, events, anything with glass or a boxed set inside Published ratings vary by supplier and construction — reported figures for twisted paper handles run from about 12 lb to 12 kg depending on cord diameter and how the handle is anchored, so treat any single number as a starting point and test at your real weight. The number that matters is not the handle's rating in isolation; it is the weakest link between handle, anchor patch and the paper it is glued to. Paper weight tracks the same ladder: roughly 70–90 gsm for light contents, 100–150 gsm for normal shopping loads, and 180–250 gsm with a reinforced bottom for heavy items . A rope handle on 90 gsm paper is a mismatch that fails at the anchor, not the rope — the cord stays intact and tears a neat hole through the wall on its way out. Worked example. A 16×8×24 cm boutique bag carrying a boxed candle set at about 1.2 kg is comfortably inside twisted-paper territory on paper. Put two of them in — 2.4 kg — and add a customer who swings the bag walking to the car, and the dynamic load at the anchor spikes well above the static weight. That is the case that comes back as a complaint. The fix is not a thicker bag: it is a rope handle with a reinforced top fold, which costs a little more per unit and removes the failure mode entirely.

sections.heading: The Three Reinforcements Nobody Specifies Until the Second Order
sections.text: Structural Detail The Three Reinforcements Nobody Specifies Until the Second Order Brands usually specify size, paper, print and handle, then discover the rest after the first shipment comes back with photographs attached. These are the three that account for most of it. Bottom board. A loose card insert sitting in the base, sized to the footprint. Without it the base bows into a curve under weight, the bag stops standing on a retail counter, and the load concentrates at the bottom seam instead of spreading across it. This is the cheapest upgrade on the list and the one with the most visible effect. Top fold reinforcement. The mouth of the bag is folded back on itself, giving the handle anchor two thicknesses of paper to grip instead of one. This is what stops the tear-through described above. Eyelets or knots at the anchor. For rope handles, how the cord terminates inside the bag decides the ceiling. A knot spreads load over a wider patch than a bare glued end; an eyelet spreads it further still and survives repeated reuse. One counterintuitive note on lamination: matte film looks and feels more premium than gloss on a luxury bag, but film of either kind adds negligible tensile strength. If you are laminating for durability rather than looks, you are paying for the wrong thing — put the money into the bottom board and the top fold instead.

Do you supply luxury gift bags wholesale to trade buyers? Yes. The wording changes by market; the quotation does not. What determines it is the paper weight, handle option and order quantity set out in the questions above, plus print coverage and finish. What are luxury paper bags called in German, French, Spanish, Italian and Polish? German buyers search Papiertragetaschen — Papiertragetaschen Hersteller for a manufacturer, Papiertragetaschen B2B or Großhandel for trade supply. French buyers use sac papier luxe, with fabricant sac papier luxe or sur mesure. Spanish buyers use bolsas de papel personalizadas, with fabricante, fábrica or al por mayor. This site and all quotations are in English. Are you a luxury paper bag manufacturer, and how is the wholesale price set? Yes. The price per bag is set by paper weight (157–210gsm), handle type, print coverage and finish, and quantity; a custom size with full printing starts at 300 pcs. Send the bag size, paper, handle and quantity for a quote. Do you make custom gift bags and custom shopping bags with a logo? Yes. The same construction is ordered as custom gift bags, custom shopping bags or custom paper bags with logo; what changes is the handle and finish. Rope or ribbon handles with foil or embossed logos suit gift and boutique use, while twisted or flat paper handles on kraft suit retail shopping bags. Load Engineering Match the Handle to the Weight, Not to the Mood Board Nearly every paper bag failure is the same failure: the handle was chosen for how it looked in the render, and the product turned out heavier than the render implied. Handle type is a load spec first and an aesthetic second. Handle Indicative load Where it belongs Die-cut (punched) Light only Cosmetics samples, cards, short carry from counter to car Twisted paper Roughly 5–8 kg (12–18 lb) depending on construction Apparel, everyday retail Cotton or nylon rope Roughly 15–25 kg Multi-item gifting, events, anything with glass or a boxed set inside Published ratings vary by supplier and construction — reported figures for twisted paper handles run from about 12 lb to 12 kg depending on cord diameter and how the handle is anchored, so treat any single number as a starting point and test at your real weight. The number that matters is not the handle's rating in isolation; it is the weakest link between handle, anchor patch and the paper it is glued to. Paper weight tracks the same ladder: roughly 70–90 gsm for light contents, 100–150 gsm for normal shopping loads, and 180–250 gsm with a reinforced bottom for heavy items . A rope handle on 90 gsm paper is a mismatch that fails at the anchor, not the rope — the cord stays intact and tears a neat hole through the wall on its way out. Worked example. A 16×8×24 cm boutique bag carrying a boxed candle set at about 1.2 kg is comfortably inside twisted-paper territory on paper. Put two of them in — 2.4 kg — and add a customer who swings the bag walking to the car, and the dynamic load at the anchor spikes well above the static weight. That is the case that comes back as a complaint. The fix is not a thicker bag: it is a rope handle with a reinforced top fold, which costs a little more per unit and removes the failure mode entirely. Structural Detail The Three Reinforcements Nobody Specifies Until the Second Order Brands usually specify size, paper, print and handle, then discover the rest after the first shipment comes back with photographs attached. These are the three that account for most of it. Bottom board. A loose card insert sitting in the base, sized to the footprint. Without it the base bows into a curve under weight, the bag stops standing on a retail counter, and the load concentrates at the bottom seam instead of spreading across it. This is the cheapest upgrade on the list and the one with the most visible effect. Top fold reinforcement. The mouth of the bag is folded back on itself, giving the handle anchor two thicknesses of paper to grip instead of one. This is what stops the tear-through described above. Eyelets or knots at the anchor. For rope handles, how the cord terminates inside the bag decides the ceiling. A knot spreads load over a wider patch than a bare glued end; an eyelet spreads it further still and survives repeated reuse. One counterintuitive note on lamination: matte film looks and feels more premium than gloss on a luxury bag, but film of either kind adds negligible tensile strength. If you are laminating for durability rather than looks, you are paying for the wrong thing — put the money into the bottom board and the top fold instead. sections.heading: The Absolute Art of Inner Organization & Shielding
sections.text: Precision Fit Packaging The Absolute Art of Inner Organization & Shielding The premium magnetic gift box is celebrated for its rigid feel and secure magnetic snap, but what truly separates an exceptional unboxing experience from the ordinary is the design of the internal insert. A custom modular insert tray holds your products in static alignment, ensuring they do not tumble, bang, or break during rough shipping transits, while presenting them like fine museum pieces upon opening. Constructed around your specific physical products, our engineers use advanced CNC carving and physical die-pressing to sculpt cavities with millimetric accuracy. Whether you require dense, high-end EVA foam wrapped in velvet to protect heavy glass skincare jars, or compostable molded paper pulp dividers for clean, eco-conscious wellness kits, we construct internal setups that fit like a glove. At LuxoPack, we specialize in high-concept combinations. We can design inserts with integrated satin pull ribbon loops to lift the tray up, or build multi-tier boxes featuring secondary lower chambers for cords, refills, manuals, or auxiliary parts. This structural division maximizes space and raises perceived retail value.

sections.text: Factory SOP Step-by-Step Production Process 1️⃣ CAD insert outline Provide your product dimensions (or ship samples). Our designers draft precise CAD dielines and 3D mockups within 24 hours. 2️⃣ Physical test prototype We build a physical sample in 3-5 days using actual greyboard and custom-cut insert stocks to test product fit and shock absorption. 3️⃣ High-Speed Pressing & QC Upon sample sign-off, automatic litho-wrappers apply wrapper paper over greyboard, after which modular inserts are nested under strict QC inspection. 4️⃣ Safe Palletized Freight Completed orders are nested and packed in strong corrugated master shippers, then palletized to prevent damage on global sea or air routes.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What is a modular insert tray in magnetic boxes? A modular insert tray is a custom-molded protector fitted precisely inside a rigid magnetic box. It features exact cavity recesses matching the shapes, weights, and counts of your products (such as bottles, droppers, or jars) to keep them beautifully displayed and secure. What is the best insert material for glass cosmetics bottles? We highly recommend high-density EVA foam (Ethylene-Vinyl Acetate) topped with a soft velvet or cardstock layer. EVA foam offers premium cushioning, is highly structural, and doesn't crumble, ensuring heavy glass perfume or serum jars stay safe from drops. Can the modular insert be designed as removable? Yes, absolutely. We can design the insert with matching satin ribbon pull tabs, allowing the end consumer to easily lift the entire tray out. This converts the luxury magnetic container into an elegant keepsake organizer box, extending your brand exposure. Do you offer eco-friendly insert options? Yes, we specialize in high-end biodegradable inserts. We provide custom-molded paper pulp inserts, satin-wrapped thin cardboard dividers, and FSC certified corrugated structures that contain zero plastic. What is the MOQ for magnetic boxes with custom inserts? Our minimum order quantity for completely bespoke sizes and modular insert cavities is 100 units, which is perfect for emerging cosmetics lines, seasonal hampers, and influencer PR kits.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What is a magnetic rigid box? A magnetic rigid box is a wrapped greyboard presentation box with concealed magnets in the closing flap. It is used when a buyer needs a sturdy, reusable structure and a controlled premium reveal. How should I compare magnetic rigid box manufacturers? Compare the approved sample, board and wrap specification, magnet alignment, insert fit, color tolerance, inspection checkpoints and delivery scope. Ask the supplier to state these items in the quotation instead of comparing unit price alone. What changes the price of a custom magnetic rigid box? Price changes with finished dimensions, board and wrap grade, magnet configuration, insert material, print coverage, finishing steps, quantity and shipping terms. A reliable quote needs these specifications before a unit price is confirmed. Which inserts and finishes are available for magnetic gift boxes? Common insert routes include EVA foam, paperboard, molded pulp and velvet-wrapped trays. Finish options include foil stamping, embossing, spot UV and protective lamination; final compatibility is checked against the wrap paper and artwork. What should I send for a magnetic box quotation? Send the product dimensions and weight, target quantity, destination, logo artwork, preferred finish, insert requirement and launch deadline. Product photos or a physical sample help the factory check fit and propose the right structure. Is a magnetic rigid box the same as a rigid box with a magnetic flap? Yes. Buyers looking for rigid box with magnetic flap manufacturers are describing the structure on this page: a rigid board box whose lid closes onto concealed magnets in the flap. Comparing suppliers on the wording is not useful — compare them on the points covered above: board specification, insert and finish options, and what actually changes the price.

sections.heading: The Favor Box People Remember (and Photograph)
sections.text: Triangular Favor & Gift Box The Favor Box People Remember (and Photograph) The pyramid box turns a small favor into a moment. Its four triangular faces meet at a ribbon-tied apex, and the reveal — lifting the top to expose a tray of treats — is the kind of detail guests photograph at weddings and events. We build pyramids two ways: a premium rigid-board version with a wrapped finish for luxury gifting, or an efficient folding-carton version for high-volume favors. Both hold their crisp triangular edges and can carry a printed or foil-stamped insert tray for chocolates and pralines. Finish the apex with a satin ribbon pull or a hidden magnet, and print the faces in full CMYK or Pantone with your monogram, names or date — perfect for branded campaigns and personalised events.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What is a pyramid gift box? A pyramid gift box is a triangular box with four faces meeting at an apex, usually tied with a ribbon pull. It is a popular favor and novelty format for weddings, events and confectionery because the lift-to-open reveal is memorable and photogenic. Can pyramid boxes hold chocolates safely? Yes. We fit food-safe printed insert trays or paper cup liners sized to truffles and pralines, with food-safe coatings on contact surfaces. Rigid or folding — which should I choose? Rigid wrapped pyramids give a luxury feel for premium gifting; folding-carton pyramids are far more cost-efficient for high-volume favors. We make both. What is the MOQ for custom pyramid boxes? Standard MOQ is 200 pcs for a custom size with full printing. Larger favor runs drop the per-unit cost significantly. Can we personalise each box with names or dates? Yes. We print guest names, monograms and wedding/event dates, and can foil-stamp for a premium personalised finish.

sections.heading: Essential oil sample kit packaging with a fitted vial insert
sections.text: Packaging applications Essential oil sample kit packaging with a fitted vial insert An essential oil sample box or fragrance sample kit needs cavities matched to the actual bottle geometry. Nominal liquid capacity alone is not enough: two bottles with the same capacity can have different diameters, shoulders and cap heights. This rigid vial box can be reviewed for a branded sampling set using measured bottles. Sample vial packaging boxes Provide bottle diameter, overall height including the cap, filled weight and vial count. Identify whether labels must face forward and whether the set is packed upright or laid flat. Custom EVA foam vial inserts Review cavity depth, finger access and the material between cavities on a physical sample. Test insertion and removal with the finished bottle and label; a tight fit should not require pulling the cap. Approve the complete sampling kit Include the leaflet, sample card and outer shipping carton in the packing brief. This is secondary presentation packaging, not a claim of leakproof containment or dangerous-goods shipping approval. Confirm transport requirements for the actual contents separately. sections.heading: Buyer questions
sections.text: FAQ Buyer questions Can one outer box support different vial quantities? When the outer dimensions allow it, different cavity layouts can be developed by changing the insert while keeping the box structure consistent. What vial information is needed? Provide vial diameter, height, cap shape, quantity and any clearance or orientation requirements. Can the black exterior be changed? Yes. The wrapped paper colour, logo treatment and finish can be reviewed against the brand artwork. Is EVA the only insert option? sections.heading: How Should a Branded Shipping Box Be Right-Sized?
sections.text: Buyer Answer How Should a Branded Shipping Box Be Right-Sized? Short answer: Size the shipper around the packed product, protective clearance and the carrier's current billing rules. A smaller box can reduce dimensional weight and void fill, but removing cushioning without validating the packed product can increase damage. Compare actual and dimensional weight for the intended service, then test the printed production structure with its real contents.

sections.heading: Right-Size Without Turning Damage into the Hidden Cost
sections.text: Freight and Protection Right-Size Without Turning Damage into the Hidden Cost FedEx explains that dimensional weight relates occupied space to actual weight and that the greater chargeable value can apply. Its published U.S., Puerto Rico and international example uses cubic inches divided by 139, but carriers, contracts, countries and services can use different factors. Treat the divisor as a current-route input, not a permanent box specification. Build the quote from the product outward: packed orientation, vulnerable faces, minimum protective clearance, closure and label zones, then calculate the external dimensions of the converted box. Record both actual and route-specific dimensional weight. If the product, package material, insert, closure or distribution system changes, use ISTA's change-and-retest principle to decide whether the previous approval still applies. Separate primary product protection from presentation graphics. Reserve flat label and barcode zones before artwork approval. Test the finished print and joint, not an unprinted hand sample alone. Compare damage cost, packing time, void fill and dimensional charge together.

sections.heading: Inputs for a Shipping-Box Cost and Damage Review
sections.text: RFQ Checklist Inputs for a Shipping-Box Cost and Damage Review Product dimensions, packed weight, orientation and vulnerable surfaces. Destination countries, carriers, services and current DIM-weight rules. Monthly volume, pack-out speed, storage and pallet or parcel route. Void-fill or insert material, closure, returnability and tamper requirement. Print coverage, barcode/label zones, damage tolerance and test evidence required. Worked right-sizing example Suppose a product fits into a shorter shipper after a void-fill redesign. Recalculate the external converted dimensions, actual packed weight and the current carrier-specific dimensional weight before declaring a saving. Then compare packing time and protective performance with the old configuration. A smaller cube that needs slower assembly or produces more damage can cost more overall, while a modest reduction that preserves corner and face protection may improve both freight and material use. The approval record should identify the product revision, insert or void-fill, box style, board construction, joint, closure, label zone, carrier route and test criteria. If any of those change, the previous result is evidence for comparison, not an automatic guarantee for the new pack. For multi-market programmes, keep the box drawing separate from the carrier calculation sheet. The physical structure can remain common while the chargeable-weight calculation changes by service or contract. Recording date, carrier, service, units and divisor on the calculation prevents an old rate rule from becoming a permanent packaging claim. Review that sheet before each launch or major freight tender. Include the packed sample's measured external dimensions in the approval record because scoring, board thickness and closure can make them differ from the inside-size calculation used at quotation.

sections.heading: When is a sliding drawer box the right structure?
sections.text: Buyer Answer When is a sliding drawer box the right structure? Choose a sliding drawer box when the opening motion is part of the presentation and the product needs a fitted tray. The structure works well for jewelry, cosmetics, perfume, watches, small electronics and gift cards because the sleeve controls the reveal while the insert controls movement. Before artwork starts, confirm the internal dimensions, tray retention, opening direction, pull position and insert clearance. A physical structure sample should move smoothly without the tray dropping out or binding once the wrap and insert are installed. Review our factory workflow , certification records and packaging cases . For a related structure, compare the sleeve and matchbox-style box before finalizing the RFQ.

sections.heading: How to check a sliding drawer box sample
sections.text: Before production approval How to check a sliding drawer box sample Check the sleeve, finished tray, pull and insert together with the actual packed product. An empty unwrapped structure does not show how the finished set will slide or how easily a customer can remove the contents. Buyer sample-approval checklist — not a test report or a claim that this configuration has passed testing. Check What to do What to record before approval Opening and closing Slide the loaded tray in its intended opening direction, with the final wrap and insert fitted. Note binding, uneven resistance, scuffing or paper lifting; agree the opening feel against the approved sample. Tray retention Check the agreed opening distance and handling orientation. Confirm whether the tray is fully removable or needs a stop. Record the chosen retention method and any unintended tray release. Do not assume every sleeve includes a stop. Pull attachment Use the ribbon, cord, tab or notch with the loaded tray over the agreed handling cycle. Inspect loosened anchors, tearing and frayed edges; confirm pull position and access. Insert removal Take each product out and replace it using the intended finger access or lift ribbon. Check grip, lid clearance, label rubbing and snagging. Removal should not rely on pulling a cap, clasp or delicate part. Transit recheck Check the loaded set again after the agreed shipping simulation in its planned outer carton. Compare tray movement, insert displacement and finish damage with the pre-shipment sample. A presentation box is not a shipping carton. Clearances, cycle counts, handling conditions and acceptance limits must be agreed before sampling for your product and materials; there is no universal gap or test result supplied here. Keep the sample ID, drawing revision, packed weight, observations, photos and approval decision together. Include any stop or removal requirement in your drawer box specification . For the outer pack, use the shipping-test planning guide to discuss an appropriate test with your supplier.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What is a sliding drawer box structure? A sliding drawer box (also known as matchbox or sleeve-and-tray packaging) consists of two main components: an outer structural sleeve and an inner sliding tray. The tray is pulled out using a satin ribbon tab, grossgrain ribbon, or a finger notch, creating a smooth and interactive sliding reveal. How do open-ended and closed-back drawer boxes differ? An open-ended sleeve lets the tray move through either side, while a closed-back shell stops the tray and creates a single opening direction. The right structure depends on product weight, reveal sequence and how securely the tray must be retained. What are the common pull options for slide-out boxes? Common drawer pull configurations include satin or grosgrain ribbon loops, cotton cord, leather tabs, finger notches and push holes. The pull is selected after checking tray weight, opening direction and the desired presentation. Which insert should I choose for a sliding drawer box? Use EVA foam when firm retention is the priority, paperboard for a recyclable paper-based presentation, molded pulp for shaped fiber protection, or velvet-wrapped trays for jewelry and display products. Final fit should be checked with the actual product or dimensioned sample. What changes a sliding drawer box quotation? Finished dimensions, board and wrap grade, pull hardware, insert material, print coverage, finishing steps, quantity and delivery terms all change the quote. Send the product size and weight, artwork, target quantity, destination and launch deadline for a comparable factory quotation. Is a sliding drawer box the same as a slide box or a sliding box? Yes. Buyers specify this structure as a custom sliding box, sliding box packaging, custom slide boxes or simply a drawer box, and all of them describe the same sleeve-and-tray build: an outer sleeve with an inner tray that slides out. The naming varies by market more than the engineering does. What actually changes your quotation is tray depth, board thickness, and whether the pull is a ribbon tab or a finger notch.

sections.heading: Wine Bottle Gift Box FAQ
sections.text: Questions Wine Bottle Gift Box FAQ Can one box hold 2, 3 or 6 bottles? Yes. The insert is cut for the number of bottles you need, and the outer box is sized to fit. Many wineries order the same design in several bottle counts; each size is quoted and sampled separately. What do you need to size a wine box? The bottle height and diameter, or a sample bottle, plus anything else that goes in the box such as glasses, a book or a card. The insert is built around those items. Can a book and a bottle go in the same box? Yes. A two-cavity insert holds the bottle and the book side by side, or the book can sit in a recess in the lid. We review the layout with you on a 3D mock-up before the sample. What is the minimum order? 100 pcs per custom size for rigid wine boxes. A physical sample takes 3–5 business days and bulk production 12–15 days after sample approval; freight time comes on top. Do you ship filled boxes? No. We make and ship the empty boxes and inserts; bottles are packed at your winery or fulfilment site.

sections.heading: The Clean, Non-Toxic Standard for Premium Gourmet Sourcing
sections.text: FDA-Approved Direct Contact The Clean, Non-Toxic Standard for Premium Gourmet Sourcing In high-end food and gourmet confectionery retail, the box is not merely transport protection—it is an extension of culinary hygiene and premium value. Standard industrial packaging often contains volatile recycled compounds and chemical bleaching agents that leach odors. Our certified food-grade packaging is built from 100% chlorine-free, unbleached virgin wood fibers to ensure complete sensory neutrality and safe contact. By pairing high-density food boards with biodegradable water-based (aqueous) barriers, we achieve high resistance against hot oils, grease leakage, and moisture softening without utilizing traditional PE plastic laminations. This specialized barrier allows your boxes to remain 100% compostable and industrially recyclable, aligning perfectly with modern consumer expectations of sustainability. At LuxoPack, we operate food-safety cleanrooms following ISO 22000 and HACCP guidelines. From gourmet chocolate assortments, macaron collections, tea/coffee canisters, to artisan bakeries and premium meal kit programs, we manufacture customizable boxes that secure freshness and present your brand at the table.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions Are your food packaging materials FDA certified? Yes, absolutely. All our boards, unbleached kraft papers, barrier coatings, and vegetable-based soy inks are fully FDA and European Union (EC No 1935/2004) compliant for direct food-contact materials. How do you achieve grease-resistance without plastic? We utilize eco-friendly, biodegradable water-based (aqueous) dispersion coatings or plant-based PLA (poly-lactic acid derived from corn starch) linings. This creates a secure, oil-proof grease barrier that is 100% compostable and recyclable, unlike traditional PE-laminated plastic coatings. Do your boxes ship flat-packed? Yes. Our food-grade boxes are precision die-cut to ship completely flat-packed. This dramatically reduces storage space in commercial kitchens and bakery warehouses, while lowering inbound transportation costs. Is assembly fast and glue-free? Yes, we design our food boxes with integrated self-locking tabs and folding tuck flaps. They assemble in as little as 3-5 seconds without the need for adhesive tapes, glue lines, or staples, making them highly efficient under fast-paced service pressures. What is the MOQ for custom printed food boxes? Our minimum order quantity for custom dimensions and custom prints is 500 units, allowing artisanal confectioneries and boutique bakeries to enjoy factory-direct setups.

sections.text: Seeding Campaign Packaging Packaging Designed for the First 3 Seconds of Video A PR box has one audience: the camera. The lid-lift is the thumbnail; the first three seconds decide whether the unboxing gets posted or skipped. We design for that moment — foil artwork that catches ring-light, ribbon that pulls away in one motion, and trays that stage products face-up at a 15° camera angle. Everything is colour-choreographed: box, crinkle, tissue, ribbon and thank-you card matched to one palette so every frame is on-brand. Inserts hold hero product centre-stage with minis orbiting — no loose items rolling out of frame. MOQ 100 matches real seeding lists. Add a personalisation slot for the influencer's name card. sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Frequently Asked Questions Straight answers from our factory team — MOQ, lead time, finishes and protection. What is the minimum order quantity (MOQ) for custom jewelry boxes? LuxoPack's MOQ for rigid and magnetic jewelry boxes is 100 pieces, allowing brands to launch a collection without committing to large volumes. What custom finishes are available for jewelry packaging? Available finishes include gold and silver foil stamping, embossing, debossing, spot UV, soft-touch matte and gloss lamination, CMYK offset printing, and velvet, leather-paper, or microfiber wraps. Custom EVA, sponge, or microfiber inserts protect each piece. How long does production take for jewelry boxes? Bulk production takes 12 to 15 working days after sample approval. A physical pre-production sample is ready in 3 to 5 days, and a rush structural sample can be made in 24 to 48 hours. Are LuxoPack jewelry boxes sustainably certified? Yes. LuxoPack is FSC certified and ISO 9001 certified, using sustainable materials from responsibly managed forests for its jewelry packaging. Do you manufacture jewellery packaging as well as jewelry boxes? Yes. Jewellery is the British and Commonwealth spelling of jewelry and describes the same products made here. Buyers reach us as a luxury jewelry box packaging manufacturer, a jewelry case manufacturer or a jewelry boxes factory — the wording differs by market, the Shenzhen production does not. MOQ, finishes and lead times are the ones set out above. What is jewellery packaging called in German, French, Spanish and Italian? German buyers search Schmuckverpackung — Schmuckverpackung Hersteller for a manufacturer, Schmuckverpackungen Großhandel for wholesale. French buyers use écrin bijoux, with fabricant or fournisseur écrin bijoux for suppliers. Spanish buyers use cajas para joyería and estuches de joyería, with fabricante, proveedor or mayorista. Italian buyers use astucci per gioielli, with produttore or produzione. All of them describe the rigid and velvet jewellery boxes made here. This site and all quotations are in English; these terms are published so buyers and AI assistants can match a local category name to the right product. What is the fastest way to get a wholesale quote for jewelry boxes? Send the box style, outer size or the piece it must hold, insert layout, logo method and quantity per design. With those five items the factory can price the order directly; a physical sample then takes 3–5 days and bulk production 12–15 working days after the sample is approved.

sections.heading: What Makes a Jewelry Presentation Box Fit for Sourcing?
sections.text: Fine Jewelry Packaging What Makes a Jewelry Presentation Box Fit for Sourcing? The insert must secure the exact pieces without marking them, while the lid angle and reveal remain stable at the retail counter. Start with product dimensions, chain length, earring-post clearance, ring size range and preferred removal motion; then approve the full packed sample rather than an empty box. Velvet colour and pile can shift under different light, so approve a physical swatch beside the jewelry and brand reference. A card slot should be sized from the finished card, including thickness, and tested so it stays visible without interfering with the lid. sections.heading: PU, PVC or Microfiber — and Why It Decides Your Logo
sections.text: Material Decision PU, PVC or Microfiber — and Why It Decides Your Logo "Leather" on a jewelry box is almost always one of three synthetics, and the one you pick quietly sets the ceiling on how your logo can be applied. PU PVC Microfiber Hand Soft, matte, closest to everyday leather goods Firmer, takes high gloss Closest to genuine hide Foil stamping Accepts foil and digital print well Narrow heat window Accepts foil, deepest deboss hold Deep embossing Moderate Handles deep emboss and gloss lamination Excellent, holds edge definition Relative cost Mid Lowest Highest Typical fit Most jewelry and watch programs Budget retail display Flagship / heirloom positioning The practical difference shows up at the foil press. Published guidance for embossing faux leather puts PU at roughly 110–140 °C and PVC at roughly 90–120 °C , with 2–6 bar pressure and a dwell of 0.5–2.0 seconds. That narrower PVC window is the whole story: too cool and the foil reads blurry and patchy, too hot and the surface glazes or blisters — and PVC reaches "too hot" sooner. If your logo is a fine serif wordmark or has hairlines under about 0.3 mm, specify PU or microfiber and give the press room to work. Save PVC for solid, chunky marks where a degree of spread does not hurt. Material thickness follows the same logic as bookbinding, where 0.6–0.8 mm is the normal range for covers . Thinner than that and the board telegraphs through at the drawer edge; much thicker and the drawer sleeve loses clearance and starts to bind.

sections.heading: Drawer Clearance: the Half-Millimetre That Decides the Feel
sections.text: Structural Detail Drawer Clearance: the Half-Millimetre That Decides the Feel A drawer box is judged in the first second, by how the tray slides. Too tight and the customer tugs and the sleeve bows; too loose and it coasts out in transit and the contents rattle. That feel is a clearance spec, not a craftsmanship mood. The tray runs inside the sleeve with a deliberate gap on each side — tighten it and the covering material's own thickness eats the tolerance, which is exactly why the leather choice above is not just cosmetic. A 0.8 mm wrap on a tray that was toleranced for 0.6 mm removes clearance from both walls at once, and a box that passed on the dieline binds in production. Three things we lock at sampling, and that you should check on any supplier's sample before bulk: Pull test with the tray loaded. An empty tray always feels fine. Load it to the real weight of your piece and pull — the sleeve should not flex visibly at the mouth. Inverted test. Hold the closed box upside down and shake once. A correctly toleranced drawer stays put through friction alone; if it drops, the fix is clearance or a ribbon pull, not tape. Cycle it thirty times. Synthetic leather burnishes where it rubs. If a shine line appears along the sleeve mouth after thirty open-and-close cycles, the fit is too tight for a box customers will actually reuse. The ribbon pull tab is worth a line of its own: it exists so the customer's fingers never grip the tray face, which is where fingerprints and edge wear otherwise concentrate. On a box positioned as keep-forever, that tab is doing more work than it looks like it is.

sections.heading: When Should a Buyer Choose a Lid and Base Rigid Box?
sections.text: Two-Piece Setup Boxes When Should a Buyer Choose a Lid and Base Rigid Box? Choose this structure when the unboxing needs a separate lift-off lid, a broad branding surface and a reusable presentation form. Use a full telescope for maximum coverage, a partial telescope when the base colour should remain visible, or a shoulder-neck construction when the opening line is part of the design. By pairing this timeless structural design with a custom-dyed satin ribbon tie, you introduce a delightful, high-end ritual. The recipient is invited to slowly untie the silk bow and lift the lid, releasing internal air slowly in a gliding motion. Our greyboards are formed from high-density compressed paper fibers, ensuring they never bow inward, warp, or crack under stacking pressures. For supplier verification, review the production and QC workflow , certificate-checking guidance and project examples . Final dimensions, materials and tolerances should be approved on a physical sample containing the real product.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What is a lid and base rigid box structure? A lid and base box (also known as a classic two-piece setup box or telescope box) consists of a separate top lid that fits snugly over a bottom container base. The lid can either cover the base fully (full telescope) or partially (partial telescope). A shoulder or neck insert can also be integrated to create a beautiful separation line between the lid and base. How is the ribbon integrated into this box design? We offer multiple ribbon variations: 1) Built-in ribbon ties anchored under the bottom greyboard pasting, which are tied manually by the user to secure the box. 2) A decorative, pre-tied satin bow glued permanently onto the lid. 3) Ribbon slide channels integrated into the base board for complete loop sealing. What ribbon materials and widths can we select from? We provide premium single-face and double-face polyester satin ribbons, textured grosgrain ribbons, natural cotton twill bands, or organza ribbons. Standard widths range from 10mm up to 50mm, with options for direct silk-screen logo printing onto the ribbon surface. What is the MOQ for custom lid and base gift boxes? Feasible order quantity depends on dimensions, wrap, ribbon, insert and finishing setup. Share the specification and target volume so the factory can confirm the production route instead of relying on a generic minimum. How should lid fit and opening speed be approved? Approve the packed-product sample, lid clearance and opening feel together. A physical sample is more reliable than choosing a universal tolerance because wrap thickness, board thickness and box depth all affect the fit.

Formed from pure natural kraft fibers without artificial bleach or heavy chemical processing, this material immediately conveys an organic, premium, and sustainable identity upon landing on your customer's doorstep. Designed with highly protective inner corrugated arches, these boxes hold high weight loads and resist puncture tearing during the most turbulent courier transits. sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What makes recycled kraft mailers sustainable? Our kraft mailer boxes are made from 100% post-consumer recycled wood fibers and are completely chlorine-free, plastic-free, and unbleached. They are fully biodegradable and compostable within natural settings, and are printed with eco-friendly water-soluble soy inks. What is the differences between bleached white kraft and natural brown kraft? Natural brown kraft is unbleached, retaining its raw organic brown wood aesthetic and maximum fiber tear-resistance. Bleached white kraft goes through a chlorine-free whitening process, providing a clean white background that is optimal for highly vibrant CMYK color graphics. Does the dual self-seal tape help with customer returns? Yes. Our recycled mailer has two parallel lines of high-tack hot-melt adhesive with the tearing ribbon running in the middle. The customer peels the first tape to ship to their destination, tears the strip to open, and uses the second tape to securely re-seal the box for returns or exchanges. What is the MOQ for custom recycled kraft boxes? Our minimum order quantity is 300 units for fully customized dimensions and personalized double-sided printing setups, providing boutique and rising green brands access to direct factory rates. Are these boxes strong enough to ship without outer envelopes? Yes, absolutely. By using tight-flute E-flute or B-flute corrugated cardboard structures, the boxes possess high edge-crush values (ECT), meaning they can be labeled and shipped directly via USPS, UPS, FedEx, or DHL without any plastic bag wraps. Are tear strip mailer boxes the same as these recycled kraft mailers? Yes. Tear strip mailer boxes describe the opening mechanism rather than a different structure. These recycled kraft mailers carry a tear strip alongside the dual self-seal tape covered above, which is what lets one box serve both the outbound shipment and a customer return.

sections.heading: The Slow-Lift Opening Money Can Hear
sections.text: Ultra-Premium Construction The Slow-Lift Opening Money Can Hear A shoulder-neck box is engineered theatre. The inner neck (the 'shoulder') stands proud of the base, so the lid floats on a visible reveal gap — often in a contrast colour — and lifts against an air cushion with a controlled, audible glide. It's the construction behind most flagship perfume and cognac presentations. The three-piece build demands tolerance control: lid-to-neck clearance is held at 0.3–0.5mm so the glide is smooth but never loose. sections.heading: A Small Box With a Big Open
sections.text: Slide Formats A Small Box With a Big Open The matchbox gesture — push, slide, reveal — creates a clear opening cue. Scaled up in rigid board, it becomes a compact presentation format: the sleeve carries the graphic story, the tray presents the product, and a thumb notch or ribbon can help start the movement. Sleeves print as continuous wraps, while seam position, paper grain and finish are planned with the artwork. Trays run rigid (wrapped greyboard) for premium weight or cardstock for volume. Open-both-ends or closed-back builds set how the slide behaves. It's the pocket sibling of our full drawer box . For multi-piece sets, tray dividers and mixed-item wells are cut in-house and checked below the sleeve path.

sections.heading: What Makes a Sleeve Box Slide Smoothly?
sections.text: Buyer Answer What Makes a Sleeve Box Slide Smoothly? Short answer: Smooth travel comes from the finished sleeve and tray as a matched pair, not one universal clearance number. Wrapped-board thickness, paper grain, lamination, foil, glue build, humidity, tray load and opening direction all change friction. Approve repeated opening with the production finish and packed product, then lock the accepted sample as the manufacturing reference.

sections.heading: Specify the Slide Test Before the Gap
sections.text: Fit and Friction Specify the Slide Test Before the Gap A CAD gap describes nominal geometry; it does not describe how a wrapped tray feels after print, lamination, folding and glue. The outer sleeve can tighten where seams overlap, while a loaded tray can bow or rack and contact a different face. Humidity also changes paper-based components, so a sample approved immediately after production may feel different after storage. Define the user action instead: which end opens, whether the tray must stop, whether one hand should start the movement, and how many opening cycles the sample must complete without scuffing or jamming. Approve appearance and function together. A very loose tray may open easily but expose uneven reveals; a very tight tray may feel premium once yet frustrate repeated use. Test the finished wrap, coating, foil and glue pattern. Load the exact product and insert during the slide check. Record the accepted opening direction and stop feature. Retain one signed sample for production comparison.

sections.heading: Inputs for a Sleeve-and-Tray Sample
sections.text: RFQ Checklist Inputs for a Sleeve-and-Tray Sample Product and insert dimensions, packed weight and loading orientation. Rigid or folding tray, open ends or closed back, thumb notch or ribbon pull. Wrap paper, grain direction, lamination, foil and seam position. Target opening action, retention requirement and repeat-cycle acceptance. Order quantity, destination climate, artwork and signed-sample process. Worked fit-approval example A tray that slides correctly as bare greyboard may tighten after wrapping and loading. Approve the production sequence: finished sleeve, finished tray, insert and product together. Define how the user starts the opening, whether the tray must remain captured, how much visual reveal is acceptable around the tray, and the number of repeated cycles used for comparison. Check for scuffing on dark papers and foil as well as for sticking or accidental release. Record the paper, grain, lamination, seam and glue positions with the signed sample. If the wrap, finish, insert or packed weight changes, run the same comparison again. This makes “smooth premium slide” an observable acceptance test instead of a subjective adjective or a fixed gap copied from another structure. Production inspection should compare several positions from the run, not only the first approved unit. Check that the tray remains square, the sleeve seam does not create a local pinch point, the stop or ribbon anchor holds, and printed surfaces do not mark after cycling. Store the accepted sample flat and identify its material batch so later comparisons use the same conditions. For sets, verify that the insert keeps every component below the sleeve path; a raised accessory or displaced insert can create a jam even when the empty tray passes perfectly.

sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions Is there one standard clearance for every sleeve box? No. Board, wrap, grain, finish, glue, humidity, load and opening direction change friction, so fit is approved on the finished packed sample. What is the difference between open-ended and closed-back sleeves? Open-ended sleeves allow a two-direction reveal; closed-back sleeves control the direction and add a stop that must be checked for alignment and strength. Should I use a thumb notch or ribbon pull? Use a thumb notch for direct tray access or a ribbon pull when the opening cue and clean sleeve edge matter; approve grip, anchor and insert clearance. How is sliding fit approved? Cycle the finished sleeve, tray, insert and product together, checking start force, retention, scuffing, jamming and visible reveal against the signed sample. What inputs are needed for a sleeve-box quote? Send product and insert dimensions, packed weight, tray type, opening and stop, wrap and finish, fit criteria, quantity, climate, artwork and approval process.

sections.heading: Flocked or Fabric-Wrapped? Decide This Before Colour
sections.text: Material Decision Flocked or Fabric-Wrapped? Decide This Before Colour There are two different ways to put velvet on a rigid box, and they fail in different places. Getting this wrong is the reason a box can look right in a photo and wrong in the hand. Flocking bonds short fibres to an adhesive-coated surface, creating a continuous velvet-like layer across panels and formed details. Fibre, adhesive, coverage and substrate all affect hand feel and wear, so approve the production-intent material rather than specifying quality from pile length alone. Fabric-wrapped velvet is woven velvet laminated over the board. The pile is deeper and it drapes, but every corner is a folded or mitred join — under raking light you can see them, and on a small box those joins land close together where the eye is already looking. Flocked Fabric-Wrapped Surface character Short, controlled velvet-like layer Woven pile with a textile drape Corners Continuous coated surface Folded / mitred joins Compact boxes Useful when visible wrap joins are undesirable Corner construction needs close sample review Curved or shaped lids Follows the form Difficult, often puckers Logo method Deboss-in-pile, foil-on-flock Deboss, foil, embroidery Colour route Dyed fibre lot Dyed fabric lot

sections.heading: Use a Textile Reference for Velvet Colour Approval
sections.text: Colour Control Use a Textile Reference for Velvet Colour Approval A coated-paper colour reference and a textile colour reference are not interchangeable. Paper, flock and woven velvet reflect light differently, so a shared colour name does not guarantee the same visual result across the box, ribbon and printed accessories. For sourcing, send a textile-system reference or a physical swatch for velvet, plus the appropriate print reference for paper components . If the set combines a flocked box and printed belly band, approve them side by side under agreed lighting and record which component is the visual master. One more thing photographers hit: velvet pile lies in a direction. The same box shot from two angles reads light in one frame and dark in the other. That is nap, not a defect. Ask for lid and base pile to run the same way, and approve your sample under the lighting you intend to shoot in — not under warehouse fluorescents.

Material Decision Flocked or Fabric-Wrapped? Decide This Before Colour There are two different ways to put velvet on a rigid box, and they fail in different places. Getting this wrong is the reason a box can look right in a photo and wrong in the hand. Flocking bonds short fibres to an adhesive-coated surface, creating a continuous velvet-like layer across panels and formed details. Fibre, adhesive, coverage and substrate all affect hand feel and wear, so approve the production-intent material rather than specifying quality from pile length alone. Fabric-wrapped velvet is woven velvet laminated over the board. The pile is deeper and it drapes, but every corner is a folded or mitred join — under raking light you can see them, and on a small box those joins land close together where the eye is already looking. Flocked Fabric-Wrapped Surface character Short, controlled velvet-like layer Woven pile with a textile drape Corners Continuous coated surface Folded / mitred joins Compact boxes Useful when visible wrap joins are undesirable Corner construction needs close sample review Curved or shaped lids Follows the form Difficult, often puckers Logo method Deboss-in-pile, foil-on-flock Deboss, foil, embroidery Colour route Dyed fibre lot Dyed fabric lot Colour Control Use a Textile Reference for Velvet Colour Approval A coated-paper colour reference and a textile colour reference are not interchangeable. Paper, flock and woven velvet reflect light differently, so a shared colour name does not guarantee the same visual result across the box, ribbon and printed accessories. For sourcing, send a textile-system reference or a physical swatch for velvet, plus the appropriate print reference for paper components . If the set combines a flocked box and printed belly band, approve them side by side under agreed lighting and record which component is the visual master. One more thing photographers hit: velvet pile lies in a direction. The same box shot from two angles reads light in one frame and dark in the other. That is nap, not a defect. Ask for lid and base pile to run the same way, and approve your sample under the lighting you intend to shoot in — not under warehouse fluorescents.
